newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia awards concessions to two oil firms.
newsitem.headline: Colombia awards concessions to two oil firms.

text.p: Canada Petroleum International Resources Ltd and Japan National Oil Corporation (JNOC) have been awarded concessions for crude oil exploration and production projects in Colombia, the state oil company Ecopetrol said.

It said the two companies had been selected from a group of five foreign firms that bid for the right to explore the Tocoragua block in Colombia's eastern plains and the Troyano fields in southwestern Putumayo province.
These concession contracts mark the first joint ventures with foreign partners signed by the state-run company.

Under terms of the contract with JNOC, which will explore the Tocoragua block, profits from the field would be equally divided between JNOC and Ecopetrol as long as total production is less than 60 million barrels. Ecopetrol's share share would subsequently to 71 percent of production.

In the case of Canadian Petroleum International Resources exploration and production rights award for the Troyano block, Ecopetrol's share would increase after the first 60 million barrels to a total of 58 percent of production.
In both cases, Ecopetrol will cover 50 percent of exploration costs and be the primary operator of the fields.

Spokesmen for Ecopetrol could not be reached for immediate comment. But Colombia's leading daily, El Tiempo, said 17 companies had been expected to participate in bidding for the Tocoragua and Troyano fields, which opened on May 7 and attracted only five bidders.

The number of new oil exploration projects in Colombia has dropped considerably in recent years because of what industry sources describe as its unwillingness to award more favorable terms to foreign firms. -- Bogota newsroom, 571 610 7944
